_comment: B1-AC19 budget, now per-bundle (B2-AC22): the web ESM/CJS limits were pinned at their N0 (pre-seam, byte-identical-to-main) measurement; after the seam slices (N2) both grew by the seam-restructuring overhead (extra module boundaries for Scroll/TextField/CheckGlyph/TessellatedPattern/etc., not dead code) and are called out with their measurement and cause in the PR, per B2-AC22. `pinned: true` still means 'may not move again while B2-AC11 is claimed' going forward from this slice. RAISED A SECOND TIME at the internal-review-fix pass (measuredAtSlice N2-review-fixes): three review-caught WEB REGRESSIONS were fixed (TabBar's keyboard activation and scroll-padding-inline, dropped by the seam refactor; Button's focus ring persisting after mouse-leave, changed by the seam refactor) plus one native defect fix (SquareGrid's currentColor). Restoring the exact pre-existing web behaviour (B2-AC11) necessarily re-adds the handful of bytes the regression had removed or the fix requires — this is cost of NOT weakening B2-AC11/B2-AC20, not absorbed seam-restructuring growth, and is called out in the PR for owner sign-off same as the first raise. RAISED A THIRD TIME, review round 3 (measuredAtSlice N2-review-round3-touch-targets): B2-AC20/D7's `touchHitSlop` seam (platformStyles.ts/.native.ts) and the six `hitSlop` call sites it feeds (IconButton, Tabs' Tab, CollapsibleSection's Header, SquareGrid's Square, TabBar's TabButton, TextField.native.tsx's checkbox) are a NATIVE-ONLY behaviour change — `touchHitSlop` is a no-op returning `undefined` on web and the web half of every seam is byte-for-byte what it was — but B2-AC1's one-shared-source rule means the call sites themselves (one `hitSlop={touchHitSlop(...)}` prop per shared component, trimmed to inlined literals rather than named constants to minimise this) are necessarily compiled into the web bundle too; there is no Platform.OS branch (forbidden) or component-source fork (forbidden by B2-AC1) that could make that literally zero. This raise is exactly the measured delta of that unavoidable overhead, called out here and in the PR for the same owner sign-off as the first two. RAISED A FOURTH TIME, review round 3 FOLLOW-UP (measuredAtSlice N2-review-round3-touch-target-completeness): review found the ~48dp rule applied in only one place and TextField.native.tsx's own checkbox hitSlop provably unable to reach 48dp (Android's touch dispatch clips a view's hitSlop to its immediate parent's bounds), so this pass covers every remaining short interactive control (Button, ListRow's radio, TabBar's two scroll arrows, Checkbox's Row, Radio's title-only card) and fixes the checkbox by growing Checkbox.tsx's Row instead. For Button and Radio (both already call `useInteractive`/`useButtonInteraction`), the growth is threaded through the SAME `handlers` object every caller already spreads, via a new optional `HitSlopSize` hook argument that `interaction.ts` (web) ignores outright and `interaction.native.ts` alone turns into a `hitSlop` key — zero new web bytes for those two. ListRow's radio View, TabBar's two Arrow views and Checkbox's Row have no such existing handlers object to piggyback on and each still needs its own `hitSlop={touchHitSlop(...)}` line, which is the measured delta of this raise — flagged in the PR for the owner's explicit sign-off, exactly like the third raise. RAISED A FIFTH TIME, review round 4 finding 1 (measuredAtSlice N2-review-round4-finding1-touchtarget-fix): review found IconButton's `hitSlop` was silently INERT on native (its host, `Frame`, was a `styled(Text, ...)`, and Android only honours hit-area growth on a View). The fix moves `Frame`'s definition from a local const inside IconButton.tsx into the EXISTING `platformStyles.ts`/`.native.tsx` seam (deliberately not a new seam file, specifically to avoid a new module boundary/bundler path comment on web) and gives the native half a real View+Text split. RAW bytes for both web bundles are measured UNCHANGED (408692/415049, identical to the fourth raise) — the relocated declaration is the same length, under the same exported name `Frame`. Only GZIP moved, by at most 18 bytes (index.mjs) / 5 bytes (index.cjs): moving a byte-identical declaration to a different position in the file changes gzip's LZ77 match distances even when the raw length does not change. This is the smallest measured delta achievable while still fixing the defect (confirmed by testing a dedicated-seam-file alternative, which cost 55/15 bytes instead) — flagged in the PR for the owner's explicit sign-off, exactly like the first four.

preSeamReference.note: N0, unseamed native build — a sanity anchor, not a budget.
